reviews.review:
I've played through the original trilogy at least six times now... And after recently playing through it again I figured I should give Andromeda another chance. I've seen many people say that it has gotten much better since launch and while the story isn't so great compared to the trilogy, the combat supposedly is the best...

I disagree, vehemently. 

My main gripe is, it's just not a mass effect game imho. The combat is very different and I guess people that say it's better just prefer a different style of game. The biggest change is that the power wheel is gone. You can't pause combat anymore to look around, command your teammates and choose your powers. Instead it's all real-time and you can only have three powers on your bumpers (one of which by hitting them together). As far as I've been able to see you can't command your teammates to use powers... Actually in the time I've played I don't think I've seen anything to indicate that they have any at all, it's just that I've seen there is an achievement to combo with them so they must. But there is no more tactical looking around and combining powers. 

The shooting seems pretty good, but not really anything special. One other thing that annoys... They still have the weight system to hurt your cooldowns if you carry too many weapons. I started as an infiltrator (it's called differently now, operative maybe)... But if I take a sniper with me my cooldowns immediately are shot. So I end up bringing an assault rifle because with the sniper I can't use my cloak very often. This can be fixed later with skill points, but it kind of kills the class at the start. 

Graphics are pretty cool, as long as you don't look too closely at the faces (especially the Rider men look like they got a skin condition).

Controls are a bit weird and coming from ME LE it's annoying they changed everything and you can't customise the controls (not on a controller anyway). One thing that really frustrated me is that x is reload, but holding x is swap weapons and that seems to be glitchy where it triggers a lot even though I was not holding the button down. I have had so many times where I was suddenly shooting the damn pistol instead of my AR... Also pressing B is dodge, which is pretty cool... But you can't manually go into cover anymore, you just have to kind of walk into cover while having your weapon out. And if you press B you just blink forward, which has made me jump off a cliff several times. Maybe it's partly me but even after playing for 6 hours I still find the controls overly complicated and unintuitive. 

The story so far is pretty uninteresting, but this was expected, no-one praises Andromeda for its story. 

The worst part though, coming back to that this is not a Mass Effect game... They could have dropped Mass Effect from the name, changed the names of some skills and weapons, changed the models of some aliens to humans and you wouldn't have been able to tell it was supposed to be a mass effect game. Yes there are Asari, Krogan, Salarian and Turian, but they act just like humans. There is no difference, the only thing they took from Mass Effect is how they look. 

So in the end this is just a generic scifi shooter with rpg elements... It's not bad per se, but there are so many much better games, that I just can't recommend anyone wastes their time on this.

Despite being 9 years old, the game still looks good. It's a good game with a great shooting system. Unfortunately, because EA didn't let us finish the game because they wanted to get their hands on the players' money "already", the game is unfinished. We only have two new races that inhabit an entire new galaxy. The animals on each planet are the same and there are only a few of them. Even though there are more - than +, it is worth playing.

It’s honestly hard for me to review this game because I started playing it right after finishing the Mass Effect trilogy. I was still emotionally attached to the characters and the whole universe and didn’t want it to end, like an addict taking a weaker drug just to slowly come off the stronger one.

The graphics are beautiful, and the gameplay is solid. There are multiple class/playstyle variations again, but system is more flexible, you’re not locked into one class and can switch profiles depending on your skills.
I do have to say the game felt a bit bloated in terms of exploration and missions. There’s a lot of filler content. Personally, I didn’t mind it too much and ended up completing everything, but I know other people found it repetitive. The game also has several easter eggs connecting it to the original trilogy, references to the Milky Way, mentions of Shepard, audio logs hinting at Liara work as an information broker, Krogan settling on a New Tuchanka, and N7 gear.

As for the story… I’ll be honest, the new Angara race didn’t fully click with me. Something about them felt a bit off, and the whole plot sometimes came across more like a side story rather than a strong main narrative driving the universe forward. The dialogue also lacked the weight and emotional punch of the original Mass Effect games. It felt a bit flat at times. And don't get me started on Liam... he’s the one character I genuinely avoided talking to whenever possible. I don’t think I’ve seen a more poorly written character in the series. It almost felt like a self insert by a developer or something because of how annoying he was. The storyline involving the Jardaan, the Remnant, and the Kett felt somewhat unfinished, becuase they teased a sequel, but since that clearly not happening, the overall narrative ends up feeling a bit underwhelming.

The game isn’t bad by any means. If you enjoyed the Mass Effect trilogy or sci-fi exploration games in general, you’ll probably have a good time here too. Just don’t expect the same level of storytelling, character depth, and emotional impact as the original trilogy.

I've been playing this game on the steam deck LCD. It has and install size of about 55 gig. It plays on the steam deck with some minor annoying issues. Mostly with very long load times and the EA app login every time the game is loaded.

But let's start with the good stuff. The game runs on the steam deck perfectly fine minus the load times. It has native control support without needing to tweak anything to make it work. So that's good. The graphics are really good and the game looks good.

But mechanically it doesn't play Super well. One thing that's worth mentioning right off the bat is that the game doesn't let you manually save in most cases. I've played it for a couple of hours and it has not given me any opportunity to manually save while I've played. And I've tried over and over and over but it won't let me do it.

That is enough reason Right there for me not to play this game.
The story is nothing all that great and nothing I haven't seen before in other games. It's a similar sort of plot to That in the outerworlds.

Based on the amount of time that I played so far I don't really like this game much at all. I definitely do not recommend it.
And I said that as someone who really enjoyed Mass Effect legendary edition. But this game is Just two different and is not enough like the previous Mass Effect games to make me want to play it
